title: Here's This Week's Free Game From The Epic Games Store On Mobile
description: For the last couple of years, the Epic Games Store has given away free games every week through its PC storefront. With the company having launched its own mobile store, it has also started a second free games program on iOS and Android devices, kicking things off with a curated library of titles and weekly freebies. The app also features mobile versions of Fortnite, Fall Guys, and Rocket League Sideswipe. To access these games you will need to create a free Epic account and install the free Epic Games Store mobile app and log in with your account, but once you do, you can start claiming your free games every Thursday through it. One other thing to note is that Android users can access the app via Android-based emulation devices like Retroid Pocket, as they aren't limited to just smartphone and tablets. Download the Epic Games Store Mobile app For now, only iOS users in the European Union can install the app, but the app is available worldwide to Android device users and they have a wider selection of games to choose from in comparison. Like its PC counterpart, you'll have one week to grab each game that's offered. Here's a closer look at what you can grab this week, and what the current mobile games library has to offer. You can also explore what the free PC games are this week on the Epic Games Store. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: When Is The Next Steam Sale? Dates For 2026 Spring Sale And More Fests Revealed
description: While it's always a good idea to save some cash toward the end of the month, Valve's quarterly Steam sales make it very tempting to dip into those rainy day funds. Fortunately, knowing when these sales will occur has gotten easier over time, as Valve no longer keeps people guessing about the dates. The company regularly posts dates far in advance for its sales and promotional events, and the upcoming Steam Spring Sale 2026 will run from March 19 to 26. Beyond that, Valve has also dated several other events for the rest of the year, ranging from a fresh batch of demos being dropped in the February Next Fest to a spring sale starting in March. There'll also be promotions with specific focuses throughout the year, highlighting mystery, tower defense, and PvP games. Here's the full list of everything on the way. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Screamer Shows Off Burnout-Style Arcade Racing With An Anime Twist
description: Classic racing game series Screamer is making a comeback later this year, and to set it apart from other arcade racers, developer Milestone SRL is aiming to tell a dark story that looks like it was ripped straight out of an old-school anime. Ahead of its launch, the studio uploaded a trailer showcasing new characters and several game modes, including a race against the clock in Time Attack and Checkpoint. Screamer's single-player campaign will see players take part in The Tournament, the most ambitious--and illegal--street-racing event ever organized. Five rival teams have been selected, and their vehicles have been outfitted with a unique technology that enables both offensive and defensive actions on the streets. Each crew has its own story to explore, along with unique motivations and identities reflected in both their characters and car designs. Eventually, all of these stories will intertwine together as the action heats up. Outside of the main campaign, players can take part in different game modes to test their skills. Team Races allow for ideal squads to be formed by joining forces with different characters, and the goal is to be fast and to smash your opponents off the track, as final rankings combine race positions with the number of KOs executed by each team member. Overdrive Challenge is for anyone who wants to feel a constant flow of speed, as the Overdrive vehicle performance boost is active from the start of the race, turning the event into the ultimate test of survival. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Master Chief Actor Takes A Hard Line Against AI In Voice Acting
description: For 25 years, Steve Downes has been the voice of Master Chief in the Halo video game franchise. Although Master Chief's most constant companion is an AI called Cortana, Downes is adamantly against using AI to replace human voices in video games. "I'm not a proponent [of AI]. I don't like it and I would prefer that it not be done," said Downes during a recent AMA appearance. "I've been very vocal about my feelings about the use of artificial intelligence, which on the one hand is inevitable and has many positive effects on show business and humanity in general. But it can also be a determent and it can also be something that deprives the actor of his work." In this AMA sneak peek, I talk about AI, voice cloning, and why using an actor’s voice without consent crosses a line. See the full AMA this Thursday for more on AI, Halo, Master Chief and more. #Halo #MasterChief #SteveDownes #HaloCommunity #HaloFans pic.twitter.com/jtzrxuGUcE — Steve Downes (@SteveDownes117) January 21, 2026 Downes previously spoke out about the dangers of AI during last year's voiceover actors strike in Hollywood. At the time, he said, "We're not against the use of AI; we're just against the misuse of it." Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Alan Wake 2 Studio Says Deal With Epic Was "Very Fair" After Baldur's Gate Boss Speaks Out
description: Remedy has released a new statement in support of Epic Games, praising the company for funding Alan Wake 2 after a prominent developer criticized the kinds of deals that Epic does with developers. In a post on social media, Remedy said, "There would be no Alan Wake 2 without Epic Publishing." As announced a long time ago, Epic Games funded Alan Wake 2 with the agreement being that once development and publishing costs were made back, further revenue would be split between Epic and Remedy. Alan Wake 2 finally recouped its development costs in 2025. Remedy's statement added, "The publishing deal with Epic was very fair to Remedy. While these complex deals can often take even a year to reach their conclusion, and may not always be fair to the developer, this one was." Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Lego Batman: Legacy Of The Dark Knight Once Again Ditches Online Co-Op
description: The sequel to 2014's Lego Batman 3: Beyond Gotham, Legacy of the Dark Knight, won't feature online cooperative play in a move that mirrors another Lego game developer TT Games made in 2022. As spotted by Prima Games, publisher Warner Bros. Games posted an FAQ on its official support page. There, the publisher explained a bunch of stuff, from the content the game will have to whether the characters will be customizable. Deep within the FAQ was a question about whether the forthcoming Lego Batman game will include online co-op, to which Warner Bros. Games answered with a resounding "no" in so many words. "Fans of all generations will be able to enjoy the game solo or team up with a friend or family member through two-player local couch cooperative gameplay only," the FAQ reads. "Online co-op will not be available." Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Grand Theft Auto Meets The Dark Ages In This Week's Epic Games Store Freebie
description: The Epic Games Store continues to give away a free game each week, and this week is another nice find with a price that can't be beaten. Every Thursday at 8 AM PT / 11 AM ET, Epic offers at least one free PC game (and sometimes even as many as two or three). All you need to do to claim the free games is create a free Epic account and enable two-factor authentication. You have a week to add the freebies to your library before the new one(s) take their place. At this point, Epic has given away hundreds of free games, and there's no sign that the program will stop any time soon. The company has also extended its freebies to Android devices, and you can claim a free game every week here as well. We keep this article up to date weekly to highlight both the current free games and next week's offerings. title: Tomb Raider's Sophie Turner Says Her Lara Croft Is Not A "Sex Bombshell"
description: Sophie Turner will play Lara Croft in the upcoming Prime Video Tomb Raider TV series, and now she's shared more details about her take on the character, saying she won't aim to be a "sex bombshell." "It's about her and her story and what drives her, rather than what so many people also love about her, which is how hot she is in the games and the movies," Turner told the LA Times. "But I really want to show the other side. She's so unashamedly capable. She is not a woman who hides her strengths at all." Also in the interview, Turner said her extensive physical training for Tomb Raider has allowed her to feel feel more confident taking her children on walks in London as a single mother. Continue Reading at GameSpot

title: Mario Kart World's Knockout Tour Just Got More Intriguing With New Update
description: Nintendo has introduced team battles for Mario Kart World's Knockout Tour with a free new update. The mode previously only allowed for solo competition, but now offers three different options for cooperative contests: two teams of 12, three teams of eight, or four teams of six. It's available in local or online multiplayer. Knockout Tour made its debut with Mario Kart World, as it's a new mode not previously seen in the long-running franchise. The race sees players battling 23 other characters over a long stretch, with checkpoints taking out four contestants at a time. It feels like being in the middle of a chase from Mad Max: Fury Road at points. With Knockout Tour's team battles, each person on the team gets a point based on their finish. First-place winners will receive 50 points, while anyone who can't get past the initial checkpoint will only get one point. Obviously, the total score added up from the entire team decides final placement. Continue Reading at GameSpot
